tests.title: Assistance Dogs & Accessibility Duties — Mock Test 1

questions.question: Assistance dogs in licensed taxis and PHVs must be:
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to refuse or charge extra for assistance dogs.

questions.question: Refusing an assistance dog without a valid medical exemption is a:
options: Criminal offence under the Equality Act 2010
questions.explanation: Both the driver and operator can be prosecuted.

questions.question: A medical exemption certificate must be:
options: Issued by a doctor and approved by the licensing authority
questions.explanation: Only TfL/local authority-approved exemptions are valid.

questions.question: Wheelchair-accessible vehicles must:
options: Carry wheelchair users where reasonably possible
questions.explanation: Sections 165 and 167 of the Equality Act 2010 set duties on drivers.

questions.question: When carrying a wheelchair user, the driver should:
options: Provide reasonable assistance with boarding and securing
questions.explanation: Reasonable assistance is required at no extra cost.

questions.question: If you have an exemption, you must:
An assistance dog is best described as:
options: A trained dog supporting a disabled person's independence
questions.explanation: They are highly trained working dogs.

questions.question: Charging extra to clean after an assistance dog is:
questions.explanation: Extra charges for assistance dogs are unlawful.
